open_items.area: Internal rates charge and its reversal sit on two document files, so the pairing test misses them
open_items.action: GJ080565 'Reverse August' (document file 1253855) and GJ080566 '2027-1 - Internal Rates - S12' (document file 1253860) are the two halves of one same-day posting on the same cost centre, account and PK, and net to $0.00 inside FY2026/27. The unpaired-accrual test pairs within a document file, so it reads 1253855 as unpaired and ranks it Pull value High. Extend the test to pair across document files on equal and opposite amount, same account and PK, and same posting date, and re-rank; the two reconstructions in this batch are the evidence.

open_items.area: Poolshop August repair line is $1.00 where July is $370.00
open_items.scope: Park Services and Water Parks, 73123 Maintenance Services
open_items.action: The July Poolshop split (GJ080687, INV-5621) carries 'Repair and Service Parts monthly period 100mm valve at Logan Gardens' at $370.00; the August split (GJ080788, INV-5668) carries 'Repair and service parts Aug-2026' at $1.00 against the same PK000022. Both splits reconcile to their own invoice, so nothing is out; ask Water Parks whether the August line is a nominal placeholder or the actual August charge before the 73123 monthly run rate is set off it.

open_items.area: Plant hire billing narration spans thirteen months
open_items.action: Every leg of GJ080640 is narrated 'Plant Hire Billing From 01-Jul-2025 to 31-Jul-2026', a thirteen-month window on a Period 2 FY2026/27 journal. The amounts are proven and tie the register to the cent. Confirm with Plant and Fleet which period was actually billed, so the 7C111 phasing is not built on the narrated window. Reads alongside the existing plant hire SLA item.

open_items.area: Urban bushland PK000385 is funded entirely by splits off other PKs' invoices
open_items.action: Across the four documents in this batch that touch 73126, PK000385 takes $22,252.37 from the four Austspray zone invoices in July and the same $22,252.37 again in August, and $2,200.93 from the two Glascott zone invoices in July and the same $2,200.93 again in August, $48,906.60 in all, and carries no direct vendor invoice on any of them. Every one of the six shares is identical to the cent across the two months while four of the six invoices move, so the shares are struck as fixed monthly amounts and not as a percentage of the work. Reconcile the amounts and their basis against the governing Tracker or contract schedule before PK000385's position is reported.

documents.question_the_register_could_not_answer: Journal_Pull reads document file 1247907 (GJ080271, 179 branch lines, -$537,525.23) at Pull value High: an accrual reversal that does not pair inside FY2026/27, to be read against 26SLACT Period 12 before any net (rule 5). The register carries the branch side only, so the liability the reversal releases and the rest of the Parks reversal were both outside it.
documents.answer: The document is the End of Year 2025/26 AP accrual reversal for Parks 4090000, DM# 19476619. 189 legs, $2,284,231.42 on each side, netting to $0.00. One leg carries the whole other side: a $2,284,231.42 debit to 27GLACT 1330-1-31123, the accrual liability, narrated 'End of Year 2025/26 AP Reversal Parks - 4090000 Refer DM# 19476619'. The branch O110-O115 share is $537,525.23 on 179 lines, 23.5% of the reversal; the capital project ledger 2-20191 takes $1,739,391.64 on eight legs (the largest being WWDP Stages 1 to 3 design and construction $1,307,377.46 and Mabel Park waterway naturalisation $276,528.94), and 1-20451-62125 takes $7,314.55. Inside the branch the reversal is spread across twelve natural accounts, led by 73212 Major Contracts $251,529.24 on 54 legs, 73211 Minor Contracts $79,568.26, 73121 Cleaning $64,235.38, 73123 Maintenance Services $54,284.89 and 7C111 Internal Vehicle $51,121.41; 49 of the 179 legs are 73535 Tollway Charges totalling $4,766.37.
documents.finding: The reversal does not pair inside FY2026/27 because it is not meant to: it is the release of a prior-year liability, and its counterparty is the G-ledger accrual account, not another FY2026/27 expense line. Rule 5 is satisfied by reading it against the 26SLACT Period 12 accrual it names (DM# 19476619), and the document now proves the whole of that accrual, not just the branch share of it.
documents.note: Document file 1247907 is Tier D on the pull list: its Document Line Table is already embedded on PS & WP v127 Journal_Sources, 189 legs. This reconstruction was audited leg count and leg amount against that embed, matched exactly, and is NOT re-captured (rule 12). It is the second export type over the same document, so the audit is on what both formats carry.

documents.question_the_register_could_not_answer: Journal_Pull reads document file 1247259 (GJ080211, 1 branch line, -$2,503.05 on 73312 Electricity, Water Parks) at Pull value High: an accrual reversal that does not pair inside FY2026/27. The register carried one credit and no sight of what it reversed.
documents.answer: The document is the Jun-26 accrued electricity expense reversal, DM# 18726262, taken Council-wide. 24 legs, $149,181.85 on each side, netting to $0.00. Twenty-two legs credit 73312 Electricity at property level across four ledgers, from 150 Wembley Road $37,701.06 and Springwood Aquatic Centre $22,577.86 down to 1-5 Jacaranda Avenue $917.67; the two debits are the accrual liabilities, 1330-1-31123 corporate $146,167.60 and 3051-2-31123 waste $3,014.25. The branch takes exactly one leg: 1-20802-73312, PK000469 Logan Garden Park, -$2,503.05, narrated at property level like every other.
documents.finding: The reversal pairs against the prior-year accrual it names, not against an FY2026/27 expense, so rule 5 is satisfied by reading it against 26SLACT Period 12. The branch share is 1.7% of a $149,181.85 Council-wide reversal and is a single property, which is why nothing inside O110-O115 could pair it.

documents.question_the_register_could_not_answer: Document file 1250757 (GJ080426) is Tier A, no attachment, Pull value High, and the one Tier A branch document carrying an unanswered question: a recode set that does not net inside O110-O115, so the balancing leg sits outside branch scope and the pull is the only way to find it (Open Item B-012).
documents.answer: The balancing leg is 1-13081-6D513 Internal Income, $603.20, in Plant and Fleet. Two legs, netting to $0.00. The branch leg credits 1-20181-7C111 (PK000012, Park Maintenance) -$603.20 and both carry the same narration: 'Cost transfer from PK000012 to PF202077 6744 2 new tyres fitted Incorrect Billing Worksheet 246F6B4600'. documents.question_the_register_could_not_answer: Journal_Pull reads document file 1259322 (GJ080788, 31 branch lines, $0.00 net on $588,686.48 gross) at Pull value High for a blank or non-descriptive journal narration: the largest zero-net recode set in the branch, with no statement of what was being recoded.
documents.answer: The narration is not blank on the document. All 31 legs sit inside branch scope, net to $0.00, and each names its invoice, its component, its source and destination PK and the invoice gross. Three vendors: Austspray, four zone invoices reversed off PK000052 and split into landscape, roads share and urban bushland components (INV-158850 Zone 1 $57,631.44 ex GST, INV-158851 Zone 2 $51,362.60, INV-158852 Zone 4 $66,937.12, INV-158853 Zone 6 $75,377.98, every one reconciling to its narrated gross at exactly 1.1); Poolshop INV-5668 $33,764.50 reversed off PK000022 and split across five PKs; and Sundai INV-1503 and INV-1504 reversed and split into mowing and fuel levy.
documents.finding: Urban bushland PK000385 takes a share of every one of the four Austspray zone invoices ($3,157.21 Zone 1, $3,454.08 Zone 2, $213.25 Zone 4 and $15,427.83 Zone 6, $22,252.37 in all) and carries no direct vendor invoice of its own on this document. The four shares are identical to the cent to those in the July document (GJ080659) although two of the four zone invoices moved between the months, so the bushland share is a fixed monthly amount and not a percentage of the work. That is the passthrough pattern: the PK's operational spend arrives entirely as a split off another PK's invoice, so its budget position is only readable through journals like this one.
documents.note: Two legs are not vendor work: a $1.00 'Repair and service parts Aug-2026' line on the Poolshop split, and a -$0.01 line narrated 'Rounding ex-GST to invoice subtotal TechOne 33764.50 invoice 33764.51'. The rounding line is self-explaining and correct. The $1.00 line is not: the equivalent line on the July Poolshop split (GJ080687) is $370.00 for a 100mm valve at Logan Gardens.
